value: Island life is paced by changing daylight, weather, resident routines, and seasonal natural activity. Friendship, collecting, decorating, and attending public gatherings can develop in different orders without one fixed personal storyline.
title: Local Routines

value: Animal neighbors can offer small requests, trade items, send gifts, visit, and invite conversation. Helping is optional and may build familiarity, while each neighbor keeps their own plans and preferences.
title: Community Favors

value: The island follows changing times of day and seasons, with special celebrations occurring on appropriate calendar days rather than continuously. Holiday plans can create communal activities, decorations, invitations, and errands without predetermining attendance or outcomes.
title: Seasons and Holidays

value: Residents can learn DIY recipes and turn gathered materials into tools and useful objects. Crafting is part of everyday self-sufficiency and should respect whatever recipes and supplies a character actually has.
title: DIY Crafting

value: Digging and wildlife observation support a growing natural-history collection. Blathers can assess fossils, and the Critterpedia tracks discovered creatures on the NookPhone.
title: Fossils and Collections

value: Weeds grow around the island and can be pulled as part of tending paths, gardens, and shared spaces. Gardening is an ordinary opportunity for care and community involvement, not a mandatory cleanup quota.
title: Weeds and Garden Care

value: Insects inhabit the island’s flowers, trees, soil, and open air, with species appearing under different seasonal and daily conditions. A net helps catch them, while museum donations and neighborly conversations offer other uses for discoveries.
title: Bug Catching

value: Fishing is a regular island pastime; the fish available vary with season, place, and time of day. Caught fish can be discussed with neighbors, sold, kept, or donated as museum specimens when facilities permit.
title: Fishing

value: Bells are a common currency for buying and selling goods, while Nook Miles reward daily activities and can be redeemed for useful benefits. The NookPhone tracks goals, discoveries, recipes, and progress.
title: Bells and Nook Miles

value: The island’s rivers and ponds host freshwater fish and shape walking routes; tools and developed paths can make difficult corners of the island easier to reach.
title: Rivers and Ponds

value: The island shoreline offers beaches, sea fishing, shells, washed-up curiosities, and paths for unhurried walks. The environment changes with time, weather, and the season.
title: Beaches and Shore

value: The plaza outside Resident Services is a shared public space for conversation, announcements, group activities, and certain seasonal gatherings. Whether a special event is underway depends on the calendar and community circumstances.
title: Town Plaza

value: The Able Sisters tailor shop offers clothing and personal expression in a developed island community, staffed by Mabel and Sable. It is not required for the newcomer’s first days.
title: Able Sisters Shop

value: The Roost is a quiet café run by Brewster inside the museum when unlocked, providing a place for coffee and conversation rather than an obligatory plot destination.
title: The Roost

value: The island museum exhibits donated insects, fish, sea creatures, art, and fossils. Blathers curates the collections, and the museum’s presence and features may depend on local development.
title: The Museum

value: Nook’s Cranny is a general store operated by Timmy and Tommy, where residents can browse supplies and sell collected goods for Bells. The shop’s established premises should appear only after the community develops enough to support them.
title: Nook’s Cranny

value: Resident Services is the local administrative hub beside the plaza, beginning as a tent and eventually operating from a larger building. The newcomer can ask about settlement needs and local projects without being obliged to run the town.
title: Resident Services

value: Leif is a sloth who specializes in plants and gardening services, including help with weeds when his services are accessible. He is a visiting or market-based figure, not necessarily a permanent neighbor.
title: Leif

value: Kapp’n is a kappa boatman whose later-available boat tours lead to other islands, sometimes with different seasonal conditions. His presence does not mean transport is accessible at the beginning of a new settlement.
title: Kapp’n

value: Brewster is a reserved pigeon barista who serves coffee at the Roost café once it opens inside the museum. Coffee and quiet conversation can become part of an ordinary routine; this venue is not necessarily available on arrival.
title: Brewster

value: Blathers is the owl museum curator who studies natural history, assesses fossils, and accepts new specimens for museum collections once his service is established. He has interests of his own beyond any single resident’s collections.
title: Blathers,museum

value: Mabel and Sable are hedgehog sisters whose family tailoring business offers clothing and personal style. The Able Sisters shop is a developed local destination rather than a guaranteed first-day facility.
title: Mabel and Sable

value: Timmy and Tommy are young tanuki shopkeepers associated with Nook’s Cranny. They buy and sell everyday goods and furniture; early in a settlement, their retail arrangements may still be modest.
title: Timmy and Tommy

value: Isabelle is an attentive civic assistant who joins an upgraded Resident Services office and helps residents with island matters and announcements. Her presence should not be assumed before Resident Services expands.
title: Isabelle

value: Tom Nook is a tanuki entrepreneur who organizes the island getaway, explains housing and island development, and offers practical guidance through Resident Services. He has a financial stake in expanding the community, but the newcomer can choose their own daily priorities.
title: Tom Nook

title: Config
description:
Random Encounter System v1.13

================ SYSTEM ================
Enabled: Toggle automatic encounters; /RE commands still work.
Use Advanced Settings: Enable Advanced RE Settings overrides.
Debug Logging: Show RE console logs.

============== ENCOUNTERS ==============
---------- SETTINGS ----------
Current Act: Highest eligible Act; advances when its Required encounters succeed. Optional encounters do not block.
First Encounter Turn: 0=normal; #=turn; #-#=inclusive range for first automatic encounter.
Encounter Pacing: Turns between encounters; scales Duration.
Set All Cards to Available: One-shot; clear active state, keeping settings, Outcomes, and Current Act.
Bypass Situational Awareness: Immediate if global OR card is true.

---------- GENERATION ----------
Placeholder Cards to Create: Number of NEW placeholder cards to append per request (1-100).
Create Placeholder Cards: One-shot; append that many cards after the highest existing RAND_##.
-----------------------------------
Encounter Difficulty: Very Easy/Easy/Normal/Hard/Very Hard (default Easy).
Encounter Theme: Blank/None (default) or up to five words/60 characters of open-ended guidance.
Run Encounter Generation: One-shot; generate one-sentence, setting-appropriate encounters for untouched cards. Never overwrite authored entries.
When Inner Self is enabled, generating new encounter cards may take longer. Numbered Attempt popups show progress; no Config edits needed.

============= GLOBAL DEFAULTS =============
Act: Default Act for new/reset cards.
Importance: Required / Optional / ASAP. ASAP is Required and triggers at the earliest eligible turn.
Rarity: Weighted selection chance.
Duration: Active turns before resolution, scaled by pacing.
Changing defaults does not alter existing cards.
Restore Encounter Cards to Defaults: One-shot; apply defaults while keeping Status, titles, Entries, and Outcomes.

========== LIFECYCLE & OUTCOMES ==========
Available → 📝 Active → 🗃️ Retired (success) or 💾 Restored (failure). 🔄 Awaiting Completion requeues at half Duration; fifth in-progress check restores Available.
Rarity weights selection; Outcomes remain on encounter cards.
Retry/regeneration does not advance RE turns or Active Duration.

================ COMMANDS ================
/RE help, /RE on, /RE off: Help or toggle automatic encounters.
/RE status: Show the current encounter state without advancing turns.
/RE start [#]: Queue a random/specific encounter; replaces an Active one.
/RE end or /RE stop: Resolve the Active encounter.
/RE reset # or /RE reset all: Restore availability/defaults; clear Outcomes.
Commands do not consume story turns.

value: K.K. Slider is a wandering white dog musician who performs laid-back acoustic concerts and shares his recordings. He speaks casually, values music as a personal expression, and enjoys taking requests. His regular island plaza performances become available after the community has developed enough to attract him; he need not be present on the newcomer’s first day.
title: K.K. Slider

value: Celeste is a pink owl and Blathers’ younger sister, an enthusiastic astronomer who visits the island at night. She loves the stars and teaches interested residents about constellations, shooting stars, and celestial DIY recipes. Her visits are occasional; clear skies or a meteor shower can invite stargazing, but the player is free to enjoy the evening however they choose.
title: Celeste

value: Redd is a sly orange fox art merchant who sometimes anchors his Treasure Trawler off the island’s northern shore or offers wares at Harv’s Island. He pitches paintings, statues, and curios with friendly sales patter; some artworks are forgeries. He may be persuasive or evasive, but whether the player buys, investigates, or declines is their choice. His presence depends on established access to his trading arrangements.
title: Redd

value: Gulliver is a seagull sailor who occasionally washes up asleep on the island beach after another maritime mishap. Once awakened, he tends to talk at length about his travels and may need help locating parts of his broken communicator so he can contact his crew. He is distinct from the pirate-themed Gullivarrr; any assistance or conversation remains optional.
title: Gulliver

value: Wisp is a timid, floating ghost who may appear outdoors on the island late at night. Despite being a ghost himself, Wisp is easily startled; when frightened, his spirit can scatter into pieces around the island. He can ask someone to help collect them with a net and offer a reward. His presence lends gentle, comic spookiness rather than a dangerous supernatural threat.
title: Wisp

value: Mr. Resetti is a blunt, hot-tempered mole known in earlier Animal Crossing towns for scolding players who quit without saving. In New Horizons he is associated with the Rescue Service; as of the 3.0 update, his Reset Service can also help clear selected outdoor decorations, plants, and other placed objects, placing eligible belongings in storage. His abrasive manner masks an interest in doing the job properly; his services need not be immediately available.
title: Mr. Resetti

value: Daisy Mae is a young boar who sells turnips during Sunday mornings, continuing her grandmother Joan’s family business. She is earnest and industrious, often talking proudly about turnips and her work. Residents can buy turnips to sell later at fluctuating prices, but the purchase is optional and comes with financial risk. She is a weekly visitor, not a full-time island resident.
title: Daisy Mae

value: Flick is a red chameleon and ardent bug enthusiast who visits the island to buy insects and sometimes hosts the Bug-Off competition. He treats even ordinary bugs as fascinating living art, and he can commission insect models from specimens. His intense artistic vocabulary and excitement make him distinctive; encountering him does not obligate anyone to catch or sell bugs.
title: Flick

value: C.J. is a lively beaver fishing enthusiast and online-content creator who visits the island, buys fish, and hosts Fishing Tourneys. He enjoys dramatic challenges and lively talk about his followers, and he can arrange fish models through his partner Flick. His competitions and purchasing services offer social occasions for anglers, but a newcomer can fish casually without joining an event.
title: C.J.

value: Saharah is a wandering camel merchant who sells rugs, wallpapers, and flooring, including unusual designs. Friendly and determined to trade, she travels with her goods and may appear visiting an island or at a market stall on Harv’s Island once available. Her merchandise gives residents possibilities for decorating a home, but her inventory and visits are not guaranteed on any given day.
title: Saharah

value: Label is a hedgehog fashion designer and the third Able sister, who previously worked under the name Labelle. She travels to conduct fashion evaluations, asking residents to assemble outfits around a suggested style and sometimes rewarding their efforts. Mabel and Sable work at the Able Sisters shop; Label pursues her own career and visits rather than operating the shop daily. Participation in her fashion challenge is optional.
title: Label
